request.summary: Create a production airport departure board backed by an editable internal table.
request.audience: Airport passengers scanning flight status from a distance.
request.primaryGoal: Keep departure time, destination, flight, gate, and status readable across signage layouts.

assumptions: The customer maintains departures as table rows and expects live edits without rebuilding the app.
Rows missing core flight identity fields should be ignored instead of breaking the board.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The board is intended for full-screen, split-screen, portrait, and compact airport signage zones.

settings.purpose: Selects the coordinated Dark, Light, or Custom color scheme.
Airport name in the board header.
Message shown when no valid departures exist.

dynamicText.fallback: At the readable minimum, keep one line and ellipsize the remaining tail.
dynamicText.rationale: The configurable board title is primary wayfinding text and should remain complete whenever the available width permits.

dynamicText.fallback: Ellipsize the destination after preserving the departure time, flight, gate, and status columns.
dynamicText.rationale: Timetable row alignment and scan speed are more important than showing an unbounded destination on multiple lines.

states.expectation: The coordinated light preset remains legible and preserves the departure-board hierarchy.
Representative departures remain visible before a datasource is selected.
An explicit empty state replaces the table body.
A null bound value remains stable and communicates missing data.
Long destinations, airlines, and statuses remain contained in a wide-low zone.
A short odd row count fills the available body without top compression.
Malformed rows are skipped while valid departures still render.
Processed row-array output normalizes to the same board model.
A large source paginates without rendering an unbounded DOM.
The final partial page remains balanced after rotation.
A datasource edit updates the placed board without rebuilding.

behaviors.expectation: Rows per page adapt to height, rotate on schedule, and fill the final page without overlap.
Datasource changes update visible flight status in place.
An empty datasource still identifies the app and states why the surface is empty, in text legible at the declared viewing distance.

visualDirection.summary: A transport reader board governed by scan speed, column rhythm, and operational status rather than card-based dashboard conventions.
signatureChoices: One continuous timetable with strong horizontal registration.
Status color is reserved for actionable departure changes.
avoid: Independent cards for each flight row.

visualReview.intent: A dense, high-contrast transport board optimized for fast scanning rather than decorative presentation.
focus: Verify the final column and long statuses never clip at any edge.
Verify few rows and partial pages still use the assigned height intentionally.
